subject.title: [Bug]: Terminal provider model_not_available in subagent announce path can trigger chat.history storm and gateway event-loop starvation

question: Which boundary should own the permanent fix for provider-terminal subagent announce failures: subagent delivery cleanup, provider/model config validation, gateway history polling limits, or a combined recovery path?
rationale: A narrow code repair risks choosing the wrong compatibility behavior because the issue spans provider semantics, subagent session delivery, config/model validation, and gateway availability.

options.title: Require combined recovery
options.body: Treat terminal provider/model failures as a bounded subagent failure that wakes the parent and avoids requester `chat.history` storming, while adding the chosen validation/preflight guard.

options.title: Land parent wake first
options.body: Accept a staged approach where #95080 or equivalent wakes the parent, then track provider/config/history-poll hardening as follow-up work.

options.title: Make config validation canonical
options.body: Prioritize rejecting unresolvable provider/model refs before runtime and leave announce cleanup behavior to the existing #90178 cluster.

recommendation.title: Require combined recovery
recommendation.body: Treat terminal provider/model failures as a bounded subagent failure that wakes the parent and avoids requester `chat.history` storming, while adding the chosen validation/preflight guard.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely owner has recent history on the subagent lifecycle/cleanup paths and is the best available routing candidate among the identified owners.
